prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor bedroom layout across 5 frames where the camera wearer pitches their head downward and turns slightly left between frames 2 and 3, shifting view from a back wall and doorway (about 2.5 to 4 metres away) down onto a cluttered bed surface within 0.3 to 1.5 metres and a mesh playpen immediately to the left at 0.5 to 1.2 metres. In the foreground of frames 3 to 5, the camera wearer's own hands and a white cloth or diaper at the bottom edge are brightest (0.2 to 0.4 metres, well within arm's reach), positioned in front of and below a grey plastic lid, an open cardboard box (about 0.8 to 1.2 metres away), and an orange laundry basket to the right (about 1.2 to 1.5 metres away, roughly 0.5 metres from the box). The cardboard box partially occludes the turquoise bedding and a second box behind it, while the playpen's near corner, the orange basket, and the wearer's hands are partly cut off at the left, right, and bottom frame boundaries. Compared to the cluttered RGB image, the depth map much more clearly separates the vertical planes of the protruding box flaps, the playpen frame, and the recessed hallway in the upper background. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 2 where motion blur flattens object boundaries, and inside the playpen in frames 3 to 5 where it renders the semi-transparent mesh wall as a solid surface that partially obscures the spherical balloons inside.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map fails completely in frames 1 and 2 due to camera angle and motion blur, before partially capturing the foreground bed and playpen scene (0.3 to 1.5 metres away) as the camera wearer looks down and stabilizes the view across frames 3 to 5. In frame 3, it detects the camera wearer's left and right hands/forearms at the bottom-center and bottom-right (within 0.2 to 0.4 metres, facing away from the wearer and within arm's reach of the bedding) as 'person' masks, alongside a blue balloon inside the playpen about 1.0 metre to the left that is misclassified as an 'apple' and separated from the hands by about 0.8 metres. In frames 4 and 5, it segments the playpen on the left (0.5 to 1.2 metres away) and the mattress with turquoise blankets in the center-right (0.4 to 1.5 metres away) as multiple overlapping 'bed' instances, while labeling a small dark object on the mattress at 0.5 metres (within arm's reach) as a 'remote' in frame 4. When overlaid with the RGB context, the contiguous masks in frames 4 and 5 help delineate the overall surface extent of the bed and playpen despite heavy occlusion from the unsegmented cardboard box, grey lid, and orange basket resting on top. Overall, the map is highly unreliable, missing all objects in the first two frames, dropping the wearer's hands after frame 3, and producing fragmented, flickering boundaries with false class labels like 'apple' and 'remote'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is mostly blank across the 5 frames, containing only one genuine magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand at the bottom-center of frame 3 (about 0.3 metres away, within arm's reach of the white cloth and bed surface) as the wearer tilts their head down from the wall toward the bed. It also plots three false-positive yellow body skeletons on background clutter: one on the far left of frame 1 inside the playpen (about 1.2 metres away), one at the bottom-left of frame 2 on the blurred cardboard box (about 0.9 metres away), and one at the bottom-left of frame 4 on the bed surface (about 0.7 metres away, roughly 0.5 metres left of the center). Because no other people are actually present in the room, there are no true faces or gazes directed toward or away from the camera wearer, though the hallucinated skeletons in frames 1 and 4 include false head keypoints above torso boxes oriented roughly toward the camera. In frame 3, the magenta hand skeleton provides precise finger joint positions and an open-palm orientation reaching leftward that are difficult to resolve in the RGB frame due to motion blur and partial cutoff at the bottom edge. Otherwise, the pose map is largely unreliable, hallucinating human torsos on boxes, blankets, and playpen struts while failing to detect the camera wearer's left hand in frames 3 to 5.
